statement: Let $f(x)=x^{2}+1$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{x-1}$ for $x\ge1$. Find $f(g(x))$ and $g(f(x))$, stating the domain of each.
solution:
$$f(g(x))=(\sqrt{x-1})^{2}+1=(x-1)+1=x,$$
with domain $x\ge1$ (the domain of $g$).
$$g(f(x))=\sqrt{(x^{2}+1)-1}=\sqrt{x^{2}}=|x|.$$
Since $f(x)=x^{2}+1\ge1$ for all real $x$, the input to $g$ is always valid, so the domain of $g(f(x))$ is all real $x$.
hints: Substitute g(x) into f, and f(x) into g.
Simplify the square root of a square carefully.
Check where each inner function is defined.
